correctness.rationale: The weight-minus-one affine identity is expanded directly and its constant, linear and bilinear terms are separated. This yields R²=R, Rp=0, the Lie-subalgebra projection condition, and [p,Im R] contained in Im R. Every line/plane and every permissible automorphism of the Heisenberg Lie algebra is classified; the six orbit representatives are exhaustive and inequivalent. The finite-field orbit census follows from q+1 central planes and q² lines complementary to each plane, and checker reproduces q=3 exhaustively and q=5 partially.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary theorem characterizes canonical affine operators through Lie subalgebra pairs and translations but classifies equivalence only in dimension at most two. Existing 2018/2024 Heisenberg classifications concern linear operators rather than the affine center-translation group action. The six affine orbits and all finite-field orbit sizes are obtained by additional complete ordered-plane geometry and stabilizer analysis. A hidden equivalent derivation from earlier linear classifications remains a named risk.

value.rationale: A complete classification of the first three-dimensional nonabelian canonical Lie affgebra naturally extends the new affine Rota–Baxter factorization theory beyond its at-most-two-dimensional equivalence tables. It resolves all orbit types and supplies an exact distribution over every odd finite field, revealing precisely how central translation and Heisenberg subalgebra geometry eliminate or preserve parameters.
